items.title: 61124_Mario Bauza oral history interview
items.q: I got a piano player that just came out of Juillard, this lady got a choir from the Juillard. So we combined all that

ctx.x: Jomana Alfarro from Cuba. I got a piano player that just came out of Juillard, this lady got a choir from the Juillard. So we combined all that (inaudible). That was the biggest explosion you ever see in New York City. On Channel two and Channel 37, they were supposed to come on with the news. I don't know what happened. (Unintelligible). The New York Times said, the first time in history, (unintelligible).

Yeah. I've noticed -- I mean, it seems to be a permanent problem in that you've got anywhere between one and seven and one and ten New Yorkers, depending on who you believe is Spanish-speaking, about one in 7.5. And yet, I mean, I've noticed the Latin musicians are what you might call the invisible men of American music. Take yourself, -- I mean, the musicians know you but when I talk to jazz people, they don't know anything about it.
